facts.raw_span: A 19-year-old female student
weight: 35 kg, height: 159 cm
grade III dyspnea
prescribed diuretics (spironolactone–torsemide combination) and aspirin post-surgery
bouts of an extremely stiff, nonpainful neck that tilted her head involuntarily leftwards, upwards, and backwards in hyperextension
Conjugate deviation of the eyes upward or laterally
Involuntary posturing with head, neck, and spine arched backward
Difficulty in opening or closing the mouth
Echocardiographic evaluation showed subpulmonic ventricular septal defect, severe aortic regurgitation due to right coronary cusp prolapse, and dilated left ventricle with ejection fraction of 40%
Post-repair transesophageal echocardiographic assessment showed mild aortic regurgitation
Blood chemistry and electrolyte levels were within normal limits
